title: Position- based pelvimetry in pregnant women in the third trimester: A prospective MRI-based study to measure pelvic dimensions
summary:
This study investigates how mobile the pelvis of pregnant women is in the third trimester of pregnancy and how different body positions affect the pelvic shape. With the help of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), pelvic measurements relevant to childbirth are being compared in different positions for the first time. 

The aim is to gain a better understanding of how the pelvis can adapt during labour. This should enable more precise assessments to be made as to when a natural birth is safe, even if the child is in a breech position. In the long term, this could avoid caesarean sections, reduce risks for mother and child and improve individual birth planning.

interventions.name: First-time pregnant women in the 34th - 36th week of pregnancy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- BMI: 18.5 - 30
- Pregnant women in the 34th - 36th week of pregnancy
- First-time mothers
- Single pregnancy
- Fetus in breech presentation
- Estimated minimum foetal weight ≥ 2500 g
- Adequate foetal weight gain
- Consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of consent
- Multiple pregnancies
- Known malformations of the pelvis, spine and uterus
- Previous pelvic operations
- Growth retardation of the foetus (<10th percentile)
- Contraindications for MRI (e.g. metal implants, claustrophobia)
- Pre-existing or obstetrically relevant diseases (e.g. diabetes, pre-eclampsia)
